Approval basis per issue: linear-done (older, transitioned) or landed-test-passed (landed on main through a TEST-passed supervisor loop 2026-09-19..23; the Linear Done transition is queued behind the pending push decision). issues.title: supervisor-spawn pins the REVIEW worktree at base revision instead of the DEV candidate
issues.dodApprovedBasis: landed-test-passed (Linear Done transition queued behind push)
issues.description:
Found by REVIEW during FOC-400 (candidate 76f0e5d, review round 1).

`supervisor-spawn.mjs` starts the REVIEW child in a worktree checked out at the **base** revision; the reviewer must manually detach-checkout the DEV candidate before reviewing (`git checkout <candidate>`), and nothing fails if it forgets — it would review the wrong tree.

**Scope:** REVIEW spawns should land on the candidate tip (or accept an explicit `--candidate <sha>` that spawn resolves), fail closed if the branch is missing, and state in the spawn result which revision the reviewer is on.

Parent epic: FOC-380.

issues.title: mcp: protocol/CLI consistency - stale zero-dep comment, dead enum kinds, silent --mode fallback
issues.description:
**Source:** FOC-401 review round 2 (nit-class follow-up).

Three protocol/CLI consistency nits in `scripts/mcp/`:

1. `scripts/mcp/jsonrpc.mjs:1,50-61` — header comment still claims "zero-dependency" while the family now depends on ajv.
2. `scripts/mcp/steps.mjs:87,160-164` — dead enum kinds that no step ever produces: remove them or implement the step that produces them.
3. `scripts/mcp/shadow-run.mjs:207-208` — `--mode` falls back silently on an unknown value; fail loudly with a usage error instead.

**Deliverable:** all three, in one change, with tests updated where they pin the current behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-1:** no file in `scripts/mcp/` claims "zero-dependency"/"zero runtime deps" in comments or docs — the ajv dependency is stated where the claim lived (`scripts/mcp/jsonrpc.mjs:1,50-61`), phrased as "zero deps except ajv" or equivalent.
* **AC-2:** no dead enum kinds remain in `scripts/mcp/steps.mjs:87,160-164` — every kind the type/enum exposes is either produced by a step or removed together with its handling branches.
* **AC-3:** `scripts/mcp/shadow-run.mjs --mode <unknown>` exits non-zero with a usage error naming the valid modes — no silent fallback to a default.
* **AC-4:** tests updated where they pinned the old behavior; the full suite in a clean worktree is green; `node scripts/lint.mjs` exit 0.

## Definition of done

* One commit on the candidate branch containing all three fixes (+ tests), lint 0, suite green, diff limited to `scripts/mcp/**` and its tests.

issues.title: mcp: scrub + truncate provider error text in typed error results
issues.description:
**Source:** FOC-401 review round 2 (nit-class follow-up, defense-in-depth).

Error paths echo provider error text into typed error results without scrubbing or truncation. Provider-side messages can be long, unstructured, and may quote request content (headers, URLs) back at the caller.

**Ground truth as of 2026-09-21** (line numbers from the original filing have drifted):

* `scripts/mcp/envelope.mjs:146` — the non-TypedError catch-all echoes `err?.message || String(err)` into the typed error envelope, unscrubbed and untruncated. Main echo path.
* `scripts/mcp/provider-jev.mjs:77-80` (filed as `:99`; code moved) — the network-failure reason echoes `err?.message || "network error"` into a `TypedError("provider_error", ...)`. The HTTP path is already clean (status only, never the body — invariant to preserve, see the header comment at `:30-33`).
* `scripts/mcp/jsonrpc.mjs:89-91` — the JSON.parse error detail is ALREADY truncated to 120 chars but NOT scrubbed (V8 parse errors can quote fragments of the malformed line).

**Deliverable:** scrub key-shaped substrings (Authorization, tokenized URLs, `sk`-style keys) and truncate long provider messages before they reach typed error results, logs, or artifacts. Add reject-path tests exercising the scrub. Keep the fail-closed semantics unchanged — this is defense-in-depth, not a behavior change.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-1 — one scrub helper, no new deps:** a single scrub function (builtins-only, shared by all call sites; no new npm dependency) that removes/masks key-shaped substrings: `Authorization`/`Bearer` header values, tokenized URL query params (`token=`, `key=`, `api_key=`, `apikey=`), and `sk`-style API keys (incl. `sk-or-v1-…`). One implementation, exported and unit-testable.
* **AC-2 — one truncation cap:** provider-originated text entering a typed error envelope is truncated at a single documented cap; the existing 120-char parse-detail truncation in `jsonrpc.mjs` is kept or folded into the same constant (state which).
* **AC-3 — fail-closed semantics unchanged:** error codes unchanged (`ERROR_CODES` intact), envelope shape unchanged (`{ok:false, error:{code,message}}`), `provider-jev` stays status-only on HTTP errors and keeps its "never echoes response bodies" header-comment claim accurate. Scrub/truncate may only remove or mask text, never add or re-route.
* **AC-4 — sweep:** grep `scripts/mcp/**` and `scripts/decision-call.mjs` for any other site echoing provider/network text into error envelopes, stderr logs, or artifacts; each additional site fixed the same way or explicitly reported clean (with evidence).
* **AC-5 — reject-path tests:** tests exercising the scrub and truncation through the real paths — a crash-throwing provider (envelope catch-all), a network-error fetch impl (provider-jev), a malformed JSON line (jsonrpc) — asserting provider text is scrubbed/truncated AND the fail-closed shape is intact.
* **AC-6 — docs in sync:** if `docs/mcp-decision-steps-catalog.md` describes the error-path behavior, update it to match what the code now does (no drift of the kind FOC-416/FOC-441 caught).

## Definition of done

* One commit: `fix(mcp): scrub + truncate provider error text in typed error results (FOC-417)` + `Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>` trailer.
* Full suite green from the worktree (`node --test scripts/` — quote the pass count); `node scripts/lint.mjs` exit 0.
* `npm ci` in the child worktree before the suite (ajv needed by envelope tests).

issues.title: docs: mcp-decision-steps-catalog.md:155 mirrors the pre-FOC-416 steps.mjs enum

issues.title: mcp: scrub the describe() schema-path echo + catalog wording precision (post-FOC-417 nits)
issues.description:
**Source:** FOC-417 review + test nits (run `2026-09-21T13-04-39-679-supervisor-c8c3`) — all
non-blocking there, collected here as one defense-in-depth follow-up.

1. `describe()` **schema-path echo (the substance).** `scripts/mcp/envelope.mjs:76-77`
   `describe()` joins `e.instancePath` into `invalid_input`/`schema_invalid` messages without
   scrub or cap. The path segments are caller-driven property NAMES — a long or key-shaped
   JSON key in the input reaches the typed error message verbatim. Pre-existing (outside
   FOC-417's scope, which covered provider-originated text). Fix: route the schema-error
   summary through `scripts/mcp/scrub.mjs` (scrub + the single `MAX_ERROR_TEXT` cap) at both
   call sites — `envelope.mjs:136` (invalid_input) and `envelope.mjs:172` (schema_invalid).
   Add a reject-path test exercising a long/key-shaped property name.
2. **Catalog wording precision.** `docs/mcp-decision-steps-catalog.md` § Security notes
   (\~:396-397) says "Every message on an error path additionally goes through
   `scripts/mcp/scrub.mjs`" — mechanically inaccurate: own-composed messages (schema paths,
   `unknown tool`, HTTP status/timeout) do not call scrub. Reword to "every
   provider-originated message". Same file § Shared envelope under-enumerates the
   provider-originated text sources (the catch-all crash echo and provider TypedError
   messages are also scrubbed) — underclaim in the safe direction; align the enumeration.

**AC:**

* AC-1 — `describe()` output is scrubbed + capped at both call sites; reject-path test with a
  long/key-shaped property name asserts the message is scrubbed/≤cap and the envelope shape
  is intact.
* AC-2 — catalog § Security notes + § Shared envelope wording matches the code exactly
  (provider-originated only).
* AC-3 — suite green via `node scripts/test-all.mjs`; `node scripts/lint.mjs` exit 0.

**DoD:** one commit `fix(mcp): scrub schema-path echo + catalog wording precision (FOC-44x)`

* `Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>` trailer. (Issue ID: FOC-443 — use it
  in the commit message; filed as a child of FOC-401.)

issues.title: ADR-0012 amendment: [G] generator nodes, one node contract, honest guarantees
issues.description:
## Context

ADR-0012 defines \[D\]/\[J\]/\[A\]/\[H\] and excludes open-ended generation from \[J\] (line 31). The target architecture needs small generator nodes — e.g. PLAN's Definition of Done and Acceptance Criteria — each one API call with minimal context. Three corrections found by the 2026-09-21 review:

* line 29 says hallucination is "mathematically impossible" in a typed output — a typed output guarantees shape, not truth;
* `decision-call.mjs` tier-2 uses `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`, whose reasoning is mandatory (measured 910 tokens / 11 s per yes/no), against the ADR's non-thinking requirement;
* tier-2 confidence = exp(mean token logprob) over the JSON answer — formatting confidence, not the probability that the decision is right.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Fifth kind **\[G\] generate-shaped**: one API call (no tool loop), JSON-schema-validated output, bounded size, only declared input fields, cheap tier by default. A \[G\] node never decides a gate — gates are \[J\], \[D\] or \[H\].
- [ ] One node contract for all kinds: id, kind, declared input fields (explicit subset of the run record), output schema, model tier, failure behaviour, where the output is written. graph.json v2 (FOC-396) encodes exactly this.
- [ ] Line 29 replaced: typed output guarantees shape; correctness comes from gates and calibration (FOC-387).
- [ ] Tier-2: a model without mandatory reasoning, or tier-2 disabled until one is measured; logprob confidence labelled "format confidence" and not used for autonomy until calibrated. `FALLBACK_MODEL` aligned in code with a test.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] ADR accepted by Mateusz; tests green; lint 0
- [ ] `docs/STATE.md` updated; comment on the epic

issues.title: Node & decision registry — every node and Jev decision is a config entry, not new code
issues.description:
## Context

Without a shared registry, each of the 28 placements becomes its own script with its own questions, thresholds and fallback. `decision-call.mjs` (FOC-386) already carries the transport. The MCP catalog (`docs/mcp-decision-steps-catalog.md`) describes steps, but only as documentation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `config/decisions.json` (or similar), validated by a schema test. One entry per decision:
  * `id` (e.g. `test.failure.cause`) and owner step / hook point;
  * questions, with `instructions` + `criteria` in a versioned file;
  * autonomy level (A0/A1/A2);
  * threshold — `null` until FOC-387 writes a calibration row;
  * fallback policy (tier-2 model / relay / fail-closed);
  * metrics to report.
- [ ] `decision-call.mjs` accepts a decision `id`, loads its questions from the registry, and records `id` + criteria version on every call.
- [ ] A0 is enforced by the loader: an A0 decision returns an annotation only, never an action flag.
- [ ] The FOC-401 steps (extraction, prompt-refinement) are migrated into the registry, and the catalog doc points at it.
- [ ] Seed entries for the W1 placements: `egress.contains_secret`, `intake.triage_node`, `intake.task_size`, `test.failure.cause`, `gate.screen`.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Tests green; docs test-count guard passes; `node scripts/lint.mjs` 0
- [ ] Every decision goes through the registry (FOC-448 (J1)) and lands in the decision log (FOC-449 (J2))
- [ ] `docs/STATE.md` updated; comment on the Jev sub-epic

<!-- fenix-roadmap-2026-09-21 -->

## Fenix roadmap (2026-09-21)

**Minimal scope.** Entries only for the PLAN graph nodes and FOC-391. The same registry holds \[G\] node configs (prompt, schema, input fields, tier). No speculative entries for later placements.

issues.title: Node I/O log — full input, output, cost and actual outcome as the label
issues.dodApprovedBasis: landed-test-passed (Linear Done transition queued behind push)
issues.description:
## Context

The FOC-386 shadow log (`.state/runs/<LA_RUN_ID>/decisions.jsonl`) stores only a sha256 of the input, next to the answers, confidence and cost. From a hash nothing can be calibrated against new criteria, optimized (GEPA) or trained later. Mateusz's direction (2026-09-21): use Jev now, fine-tune our own models later from long-term logs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every decision event stores:
  * decision `id` + criteria version;
  * the full `state` and questions — locally under `.state`, gitignored, passed through the secret scrub;
  * answers, confidence, model version (dated build) and cost;
  * a stable event id.
- [ ] Outcome labelling: `decision-log label --event <id> --outcome <value> --by human|agent`, callable from gates, verdicts and merge results. Obvious joins (e.g. Mateusz's gate answer) are auto-labelled.
- [ ] Export per decision id with train/val/test splits, used by FOC-387, FOC-398 and FOC-399.
- [ ] Retention policy and a size budget documented.
- [ ] **Labels are actual outcomes, never Jev's own answers.** TypeSafe/OpenRouter terms on using outputs for training are checked and the result is recorded before any training use.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Tests green; docs test-count guard passes; `node scripts/lint.mjs` 0
- [ ] Every decision goes through the registry (FOC-448 (J1)) and lands in the decision log (FOC-449 (J2))
- [ ] `docs/STATE.md` updated; comment on the Jev sub-epic

<!-- fenix-roadmap-2026-09-21 -->

## Fenix roadmap (2026-09-21)

**Minimal scope.** One JSONL per run: node id, full input, output, cost, latency, and the later outcome (Mateusz's approval / edit / gate answer = label, marked as a human decision). Keyed by task and run so FOC-387 can split by group.

issues.title: Graph runner — executes [D]/[G]/[J]/[H] nodes; frontman only for exceptions
issues.dodApprovedBasis: landed-test-passed (Linear Done transition queued behind push)
issues.description:
## Context

The frontman is \~40% of token volume. Routine transitions (DoR met → DEV; verdict pass → TEST; repeated fingerprint → escalate; TEST done + clean tree → cleanup proposal) are deterministic in content, yet an LLM performs them. Moving them into code is the largest cost lever in FOC-380.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The runner executes \[D\] steps and edges from graph.json v2, reading and appending typed records (verdicts, DEV exit records, gates).
- [ ] The frontman is invoked only for exceptions, escalations and HITL relays.
- [ ] Fail-closed: any unexpected state stops the runner and hands the run to the frontman with the record that triggered it.
- [ ] Measured frontman token share before and after on comparable runs (R7b-corrected).

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Tests written and green; docs test-count guard passes
- [ ] `docs/STATE.md` updated; epic FOC-380 comment links the result

## Jev integration — plan v2 (2026-09-21)

The runner executes `decide:` edges through `decision-call.mjs` by decision id, starting with `orchestration.next_step` (map #16).

* Low confidence or a provider error hands the step to the frontman (cascade), never a silent default.
* The frontman token share is measured before and after.

<!-- fenix-roadmap-2026-09-21 -->

## Fenix roadmap (2026-09-21)

The runner executes **\[D\], \[G\], \[J\] and \[H\]** nodes, not only \[D\]. First graph: PLAN (M2). Delivery transitions DEV → REVIEW → TEST come in M4 (FOC-478) and need the DEV exit record FOC-382 — that relation moved there.

issues.title: Intake gate [J]: triage node + task size → which graph runs
issues.dodApprovedBasis: landed-test-passed (Linear Done transition queued behind push)
issues.description:
## Context

Two intake decisions are LLM-only today:

* `supervisor-triage.mjs record` takes `--confidence 0–100` as typed by the frontman itself;
* task size (small → Supervisor solo; medium → dev + test; large → full pipeline, ADR-0009 amendment) is decided ad hoc.

FOC-401 built the prompt-refinement server for task size, but nothing calls it: `.mcp.json` lists only codegraph.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `intake.triage_node` (`choice`: plan/dev/review/test/ask) plus `intake.has_acceptance_criteria` (`noul`) are recorded next to the frontman's verdict, with a measured confidence. A disagreement is shown to the frontman (A0).
- [ ] The FOC-401 servers are registered in `.mcp.json` and allowed (`mcp__fenix-decision-*`) in the Supervisor/squad settings. The config-drift test passes.
- [ ] Supervisor CLAUDE.md: every new task gets `intake.task_size`, and the suggested flow is shown before the first spawn (A0 — the Supervisor confirms).
- [ ] Mateusz's or the Supervisor's final choice is logged as the label (FOC-449 (J2)).

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Tests green; docs test-count guard passes; `node scripts/lint.mjs` 0
- [ ] Every decision goes through the registry (FOC-448 (J1)) and lands in the decision log (FOC-449 (J2))
- [ ] `docs/STATE.md` updated; comment on the Jev sub-epic

<!-- fenix-roadmap-2026-09-21 -->

## Fenix roadmap (2026-09-21)

Front of every graph: decides which graph runs and its size. First consumer: the PLAN graph (M2).

issues.title: PLAN gates [J]: Definition of Ready, type/risk/estimate, AC testable, duplicates
issues.dodApprovedBasis: landed-test-passed (Linear Done transition queued behind push)
issues.description:
## Context

The PLAN squad sets `type:*`, estimate, risk and the DoR by LLM judgement, and no one checks for duplicate issues. These are classification-shaped decisions (map #3–#5).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Registry entries:
  * `plan.dor.*` — `noul` × n: testable criteria, clear scope, enough context;
  * `plan.labels.type` / `plan.labels.risk` — `choice`;
  * `plan.estimate` — `score` XS–XL;
  * `plan.needs_adr`, `plan.security_sensitive` — `noul`;
  * `plan.duplicate_of` — `choice` among candidates retrieved deterministically (Linear search).
- [ ] PLAN uses them as A0 annotations in the plan; PLAN still applies the labels itself.
- [ ] Final applied labels are logged as outcomes (FOC-449 (J2)).

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Tests green; docs test-count guard passes; `node scripts/lint.mjs` 0
- [ ] Every decision goes through the registry (FOC-448 (J1)) and lands in the decision log (FOC-449 (J2))
- [ ] `docs/STATE.md` updated; comment on the Jev sub-epic

<!-- fenix-roadmap-2026-09-21 -->

## Fenix roadmap (2026-09-21)

In the PLAN graph these are **gate nodes the runner routes on**, not annotations. Adds `plan.ac.testable` (scores each criterion from FOC-475). A0: decision + probability shown, Mateusz approves.

issues.title: graph.json v2 — node-level graph and contract, PLAN first (design)
issues.dodApprovedBasis: landed-test-passed (Linear Done transition queued behind push)
issues.description:
## Context

`config/graph.json` (FOC-158) already holds node contracts, typed edges, autonomy policy and 9 consumers — but at squad granularity. De-monolithizing squads means refining nodes into steps.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Step-level decomposition of PLAN (e.g. dor → ac → spec → decompose → push), REVIEW and TEST, with each step typed \[D\] / \[J\] / \[A\] / \[H\].
- [ ] For every step: input/output record schema, failure behaviour, and whether the frontman is involved (the target: only for exceptions).
- [ ] Schema v2 proposal, with a migration path that keeps the 9 current consumers working.
- [ ] Estimate of the frontman-share reduction from moving routine transitions to code, based on R7b-corrected telemetry.
- [ ] Design only — no runner code in this issue.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Document merged; epic FOC-380 comment links it

## Jev integration — plan v2 (2026-09-21)

The v2 design binds every **non-deterministic transition** to a registry decision id through a `decide:` edge (FOC-448 (J1)). At minimum:

* `intake.triage_node`;
* `intake.task_size`;
* `review.depth`;
* `monitor.child_state`;
* `orchestration.next_step` (wait / resume / advance / escalate / ask Mateusz).

Deterministic transitions stay \[D\].

<!-- fenix-roadmap-2026-09-21 -->

## Fenix roadmap (2026-09-21)

Scope narrowed: **PLAN first** (REVIEW/TEST moved to FOC-478 in M4). Encode the node contract from the ADR-0012 amendment (FOC-473), including **\[G\] generator nodes** (DoD FOC-474, AC FOC-475). Every node declares its minimal input fields — context size is a design output, not an accident.
